a: Symmetric encryption uses the same key to encrypt and decrypt (e.g. AES).
Asymmetric encryption uses a public/private key pair (e.g. RSA, ECC).
AES is a widely used symmetric block cipher (128/192/256-bit keys).
RSA is a public-key algorithm used for encryption and digital signatures.
SHA-256 is a cryptographic hash function producing a 256-bit digest.
HMAC is a keyed hash for message authenticity and integrity.
A digital signature proves a message was signed by a private key holder and was not altered.
A CA issues digital certificates that bind public keys to identities.
PKI is the system of certificates, CAs, and policies for managing public keys.
A nonce is a number used once to prevent replay attacks.
A salt is random data mixed into a password before hashing so identical passwords differ.
bcrypt is a password hashing algorithm designed to be slow against brute force.
Argon2 is a modern password hashing algorithm (winner of the Password Hashing Competition).
PFS means compromising a long-term key does not expose past session keys.
Side-channel attacks exploit timing, power, or other physical leakage — not pure math breaks.
